What the market fears most is uncertainty over whether rates will be raised. When the market knows a rate hike is coming, everyone acts in advance and sells their stocks ahead of time. Once the rate hike actually happens, the market stops focusing on it. It starts focusing on the next uncertainty. So what is the next uncertainty? It is when rates will be cut. If everyone believes there may be two more hikes this year, but rates may come down next year after rising too much, then if rates are cut, wouldn't stocks surge? If they are expected to surge in the future, then when they fall this time, wouldn't people buy again? So the entire stock market, the whole investment market, is like a quantum physics world. Don't trade things that are already certain. By the time you trade them, they may already have soared, or already plunged. What you should trade, and what you should invest in, is future uncertainty. These short-term risks will eventually pass, but when they appear, they can create very good buying opportunities. Over the long term, we should still hold stocks that can continue to grow. If you are not an expert, do not invest in stock futures or leveraged ETFs. Short-term changes are too large, and no one knows what might happen. When you invest in these highly leveraged products, your money could disappear almost instantly. So the risk is extremely high. Now that uncertainty over the rate hike has been resolved, the next event is the midterm election in November. Before that uncertainty is resolved, U.S. stocks may react to all kinds of news and remain volatile. Once the midterm election is decided in November, whether Republicans or Democrats win, I believe the overall market will improve. Especially starting in late October, earnings season for the AI technology giants will begin. Will the results released in late October be good? We can look for clues at the recent U.S. AI infrastructure summit. At this summit, major AI players including Samsung, NVIDIA Marvell Salesforce, and AMD, as well as Broadcom, all took part. There was an enormous amount of information. If you still have doubts about AI investing, you must understand how AI is changing now. The first point is that the conference established a theme: "Network is the computer." AI has now become a network. Whoever can build the entire network at the lowest cost and with the lowest energy use will gain an advantage. What matters in an AI network? CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and KV cache capacity, SSD speed, network connectivity, and GPU performance. And now the AI giants are starting to focus on one question: how much an AI task costs. How many tokens can each dollar generate? In other words, how much money does it take to complete one task? They also measure tokens generated per watt of electricity. Whoever can reduce the cost per token across the entire AI computing network to the lowest level can become the AI leader. NVIDIA is the leading company doing this. Second is AMD. Third are Google, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft, which are developing their own systems. The second key point confirmed at the conference is that future AI demand will shift from training to inference. Samsung said at the conference that future AI infrastructure demand could grow threefold, while inference demand could grow one hundredfold. What does inference demand mainly rely on? Large amounts of KV cache and memory bandwidth. As inference demand grows, more memory chips will be needed in the future. It will not be just HBM. It will include DRAM, HBM, NAND, and SSDs. And so on. All types of memory will be needed. Marvell said at the summit that long-context, deep reasoning causes models to generate enormous amounts of KV cache, quickly filling up HBM. This forces the entire system to perform frequent storage operations and consumes a lot of power. So next, next, the entire memory industry may change. Overall demand will require various types of memory to be assembled into a system and operated together. Samsung is preparing to release products called zHBM and zNAND-O. The two need to work together. zHBM places HBM on top of the GPU. zNAND-O stacks the SSD's NAND dies. This zNAND technology is called HBF at SNDK. Micron has taken another approach. It has launched a new product line: a 512GB DRAM module. This is very expensive, with a very high profit margin. So from the technological advances made by these memory manufacturers, have you noticed something? The technology content of memory products is increasing. And the technologies of major manufacturers may be starting to diverge. This could lead to something important: memory chips are starting to become less like cyclical products. Each product and each manufacturer has its own solution. Once a particular solution is installed in a data center, it cannot be freely swapped with another vendor's product. That is because these AI memory chips need to be combined in different ways. The more deeply they integrate with NVIDIA and other giants' data-center technologies, the less cyclical they become. And as cyclicality declines, their stocks will be revalued. From this information, we can infer another important point: optical connectivity and other kinds of connectivity may perform very well in the future. Broadcom and Marvell are the undisputed giants. Once all these products and chips are assembled, they require extremely fast connections to link all the chips together. For AI packaging investments, besides TSMC, I have always said that Intel is the U.S. company to watch. It has support from the U.S. government. Trump meets with these AI giants all the time and tells everyone, "You must support Intel." So many companies now are placing orders with Intel, including companies such as Apple. Why was Intel's technology weak before? Because it had relatively few orders, far fewer than TSMC. TSMC handles every kind of order, all kinds of chips, packaging parameters, and so on. It has the most experience and has already fine-tuned the processes. But as long as more and more companies are willing to give Intel orders, let Intel handle the packaging, and let it learn through trial and error, its technology may be weak at first, but after more research and testing, its technology will eventually catch up. This is not a guess. It is a form of practical experience from the development of the packaging industry. My own investment style is relatively conservative. I prefer medium-sized and large companies. I do not like chasing extremely small companies. A small stock may rise tenfold or thirtyfold, but that has nothing to do with me. When it falls, it can also be cut in half very quickly. And with today's political and economic outlook so uncertain, large companies have ample cash flow and very strong earning power. These companies also have a future direction: the larger the company, and the more data centers it owns, the more revenue it can generate. Because they possess pure intelligence. So now, especially by 2027 and 2028, I think this capital, in my personal view, should be allocated to increasingly large companies, especially those that own more data centers. Why? Because the larger the data center, the greater its computing power, and the smarter its large models become. In that case, its overall revenue will be higher. A few days ago, Meta launched a new AI, Muse, and I tried it. I found it very useful. It can directly book flights and hotels for you. Previously, it seemed rather unintelligent. Now Meta is building more data centers, and making them larger. Its overall intelligence has improved. So, I personally believe Meta's Muse may become a very useful assistant. Every AI system now wants to provide personal-assistant functions, letting AI operate computers for you. That requires one thing: CPUs. I have said this many times. CPU demand may be even greater than GPU demand. One GPU may require five to ten, or even forty, CPUs before the AI can operate a computer for you. So, to sum up, there is one principle: the more electricity, the more data, and the more computing power, the smarter the AI becomes. My final prediction is that by 2027, or perhaps 2028, ChatGPT, Claude, Meta, Google, and Microsoft may not differ greatly in AI intelligence. Ultimately, the difference will not be the models. It will be the data centers. Whoever has the larger data centers will have greater computing power. Whoever has greater computing power will generate more revenue. To sum up, short-term risk events and uncertainties still remain: war, oil-driven inflation caused by war, and the midterm election. These are all short-term factors. If stocks fall, it may create a very good opportunity. In November, hold on to your AI stocks. Don't exit too early. And don't forget to claim moomoo's account-opening rewards.
